prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it. Everything
else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin corner from the same camera
position, the same wide vertical framing, the same pedestrian traffic light
on its bare grey pole with the upper round lens glowing an even plain red,
the same facade, the same kerb. The same young man in the navy blue polo
shirt and beige chinos stands in the SAME PLACE he already occupies, seen
from behind, waiting: both his white sneakers stay flat on the grey cobbled
pavement, behind the granite kerb, with the red bicycle strip and the
asphalt beyond the kerb and in front of him. Do not move him, do not resize
him, do not change what he is standing on.

THE ONE CHANGE: out on the asphalt beyond the kerb, a cyclist rides into the
crossing away from the camera -- a BRIGHT YELLOW waterproof jacket, a dark
grey bicycle, and above the collar a DARK GREY CYCLING HELMET with short
steel grey hair at the neck below it. The helmet, the grey neck and the
yellow jacket are the whole of what identifies him at this distance. He is
out on the road; the young man is on the pavement. The
pale cream facade and three or four black city bicycles leaning against the wall, well spaced along the street. Daylight,
overcast and flat.
